log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Weavile
Aurora Veil up on P1's side
Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Charizard

decisions.rationale: Lead Ninetales-Alola and Whimsicott for immediate speed control, potential Aurora Veil, and strong disruption of the opponent’s Protect-heavy patterns. Keep Gholdengo for the confirmed Excadrill matchup and Maushold for Follow Me support and flexible redirection.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Protect-heavy Rotom-Wash and Toxapex patterns can be exploited with Whimsicott’s Encore plus speed control. Mega Charizard-Y/Venusaur sun is a major mode; avoid relying on Mega Blastoise into it. Gholdengo is preferred against confirmed Mold Breaker Excadrill, while Maushold provides useful redirection support. Tauros pressures Charizard with Rock Slide but is not durable into Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump.

decisions.rationale: Weavile leads to pressure Whimsicott with Ice Shard priority and Dark STAB before it Encore-locks our win condition. Charizard follows to Mega-Y/Drought for the primary sweep engine; SolarBeam becomes instant in sun to punish Ninetales-Alola. Excadrill back provides Mold Breaker Earthquake for Gholdengo and Stealth Rock. Venusaur rounds out as a Chlorophyll sweeper in Drought sun.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Whimsicott must be eliminated early — Prankster Encore shuts down setup sweepers; Focus Sash means it needs chip before KO. Gholdengo (Steel/Ghost) walls both our Water STABs; answer is Excadrill Earthquake (Ground SE on Steel) and Weavile Night Slash/Knock Off (Dark SE on Ghost). Avoid double Water coverage. Mega Charizard Y Drought enables SolarBeam to punish Ninetales-Alola and weakens opposing Water. Toxic Spikes unreliable — do not rely on Toxapex for hazard stacking. Prioritize offensive tempo over passive recovery.

decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Ninetales through likely Mega Charizard-Y pressure while Whimsicott establishes Tailwind. Blizzard is unreliable after Drought overwrites snow, and Aurora Veil may fail in sun; speed control creates a stronger follow-up once the weather and opposing actions are revealed.

decisions.rationale: Keep Ninetales active to preserve immediate Blizzard pressure. Maushold is the better replacement: Follow Me can redirect Charizard’s Fire Blast and Weavile’s attacks, while Tailwind lets it support Ninetales before most threats.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has revealed Charizard with Charizardite Y and Weavile with Life Orb; both are fast offensive leads. Mega Charizard-Y/Venusaur sun remains a major threat. Protect-heavy Rotom-Wash and Toxapex can be exploited with Encore and speed control. Gholdengo is preferred into confirmed Mold Breaker Excadrill; Maushold provides valuable redirection. Tauros pressures Charizard with Rock Slide but is fragile into Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump.

decisions.rationale: Weavile's Ice Shard (priority +1, SE 2x) hits Whimsicott first for heavy damage through Focus Sash. Charizard follows with Fire Blast (SpA 161, SE 2x) at full power to secure the KO, preserving Mega Evolution for next turn's Solar Beam against Ninetales-Alola under Drought.

Gholdengo (Steel/Ghost) walls both our Water STABs; answer is Excadrill Earthquake (Ground SE on Steel) and Weavile Night Slash/Knock Off (Dark SE on Ghost). Avoid double Water coverage. Mega Charizard Y Drought reserved for Turn 2 to enable instant Solar Beam on Ninetales-Alola. Prioritize offensive tempo over passive recovery.

decisions.rationale: Switch Ninetales to Gholdengo while Maushold uses Follow Me, redirecting both offensive attacks away from the incoming Gholdengo and preserving Ninetales for a later weather reset. This sacrifices Maushold if necessary but creates a stronger position against Mega Charizard-Y and Weavile.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s revealed offensive leads are Charizard carrying Charizardite Y and Weavile carrying Life Orb. Preserve Ninetales when practical to contest sun with a later re-entry; Gholdengo is preferred into confirmed Mold Breaker Excadrill and benefits from Maushold redirection.

decisions.rationale: Charizard Mega Evolves into Mega-Y for Drought, then Fire Blast on Ninetales-Alola: STAB + Drought boost + SE on Ice/Fairy = massive damage to eliminate the Tailwind/Blizzard/Aurora Veil threat. Weavile uses priority Ice Shard on Maushold to pressure the second foe while foes are slowed by Tailwind dependency.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Whimsicott eliminated. Ninetales-Alola is primary threat (Aurora Veil/Blizzard/Tailwind support). Mega Charizard Y Drought reserved for enabling devastating Fire Blast SE on Ninetales-Alola. Gholdengo (Steel/Ghost) walls Water STABs — answer is Excadrill Earthquake and Weavile Night Slash/Knock Off if it appears. Prioritize offensive tempo. Avoid double Water coverage.

decisions.rationale: Follow Me redirects both attacks into Maushold while Gholdengo uses spread Make It Rain. This pressures Weavile for a possible KO and damages Charizard, preserving Gholdengo to control the endgame even if Maushold falls.

Preserve Ninetales when practical to reset snow later. Gholdengo is preferred into confirmed Mold Breaker Excadrill and benefits substantially from Maushold redirection.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Weavile Knock Off Gholdengo: super-effective 2x, strips Leftovers. Charizard Mega Fire Blast Gholdengo: Drought-boosted SE Fire Blast likely OHKOs the primary threat. Gholdengo's MakeItRain is the biggest danger to Weavile; eliminating it secures tempo.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Whimsicott eliminated. Mega Charizard Y Drought used this turn to secure Gholdengo KO; re-summon sun if Ninetales-Alola switches in later. Excadrill answers Gholdengo if it survives. Prioritize offensive tempo. Avoid double Water coverage.

decisions.rationale: Switch Weavile to Excadrill: Ground/Steel typing with Mold Breaker threatens Ninetales-Alola with Iron Head (2x Steel>Ice) and pressures Gholdengo with Earthquake. Charizard uses Fire Blast to KO Gholdengo (Fire is super effective, Gholdengo's SPA is -2, Drought active).

Prioritize offensive tempo. Avoid double Water coverage. Ninetales-Alola is Ice/Fairy; Excadrill's Iron Head hits for 2x. Tailwind has 2 turns remaining on opponent's side.

selection: Aurora Veil (your side, including ally Gholdengo)
decisions.rationale: Aurora Veil acts first under Tailwind and sharply improves both Pokémon’s odds of surviving Excadrill’s Earthquake/Iron Head and Charizard’s Fire Blast. Make It Rain then chips both foes despite their resistances and may break Excadrill’s Focus Sash, while preserving Ninetales to reset snow later.
decisions.notebook: Mega Charizard Y and Mold Breaker Excadrill are confirmed opposing threats. Opponent’s revealed items include Charizardite Y, Focus Sash on Excadrill, and Life Orb on Weavile. Preserve Ninetales when practical so Snow Warning can reset snow later. Gholdengo is valuable into confirmed Mold Breaker Excadrill, but Earthquake remains dangerous.

decisions.rationale: Iron Head 4x into Ninetales-Alola likely KOs it, removing Tailwind and preventing Aurora Veil setup. Fire Blast 2x into Gholdengo pressures the weakened (SpA -2) Steel/Ghost. After Tailwind expires, Excadrill becomes the fastest active Pokémon, seizing tempo.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Whimsicott eliminated. Mega Charizard Y Drought did not sustain due to Ninetales-Alola Snow Warning overriding. Gholdengo SpA dropped 2 stages from Make It Rain. Excadrill Mold Breaker revealed. Prioritize offensive tempo. Avoid double Water coverage. Ninetales-Alola is Ice/Fairy; Excadrill Iron Head hits 4x. Tailwind expires after this turn. Aurora Veil threat from Ninetales-Alola must be prevented.

reflections.summary: Lost primarily because the team-preview plan was poorly matched to Mega Charizard Y plus Mold Breaker Excadrill, not because of a recorded decision error. The four brought were heavily committed to Snow, Veil, Tailwind, and redirection, but had no reliable answer to sun-boosted Fire Blast or Excadrill's pressure. Whimsicott was removed before it could provide meaningful control, and Make It Rain was resisted by both remaining threats. No between-game adjustment is evidenced as helping or backfiring; the game-3 plan itself failed structurally. Not evolving Mega Blastoise was likely a major preparation and preview mistake, since it offered a more relevant Mega option into Charizard and Excadrill than the unused Blastoise slot. The registered six did get useful support tools right—Tailwind, Aurora Veil, redirection, and Gholdengo's Steel typing—but the sets and composition overvalued that support while lacking immediate damage, sun counterplay, and a safe Charizard answer. Gliscor, Qwilfish, Morpeko, and Meowstic-Female are not supported by enough supplied set information to declare a clear upgrade, though Mega Blastoise was the clearest missed option.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, question the Snow plan before changing lines: bring Mega Blastoise as the Mega holder and prioritize direct pressure on Charizard and Excadrill. Consider cutting Maushold or Gholdengo for the fourth slot rather than relying on Follow Me plus resisted Make It Rain. If retaining Ninetales, use Snow and Veil as temporary support rather than the main win condition, and preserve it only when a weather reset materially improves the matchup. Whimsicott should be paired with a partner that can immediately punish Charizard instead of merely setting Tailwind. The prior game showed that Tailwind and redirection did not compensate for the lack of a Fire-resistant or faster offensive answer.
reflections.notebook: Confirmed opponent core: Mega Charizard Y with Fire Blast, Air Slash, Solar Beam, and Protect; Mold Breaker Excadrill with Focus Sash, Earthquake, Iron Head, Stealth Rock, and Rapid Spin; Life Orb Weavile with Ice Shard, Night Slash, Knock Off, and Protect. Charizard can overwrite Snow with sun, and Excadrill's Mold Breaker makes defensive assumptions and Ground-weak positioning unreliable. Charizard and Excadrill both resisted the tested Make It Rain, while Charizard's Fire Blast immediately threatened Gholdengo and Whimsicott. Do not treat Gholdengo as a sufficient Excadrill answer without accounting for Earthquake and its poor damage into this core. Prioritize a direct Charizard check, strong Water pressure, and a plan for Focus Sash Excadrill; Mega Blastoise should be evaluated as the preferred Mega holder. Snow plus Aurora Veil can still provide tempo, but should support an offensive anti-sun plan rather than replace it. The opponent's fourth brought Pokémon was not identified, so avoid overcommitting the rematch plan to any unrevealed option.

reflections.summary: Won 2-1 with clean piloting (0 decision errors). Game 3 was decided by offensive tempo and favorable type matchups. Weavile's Ice Shard and Charizard's Fire Blast eliminated Whimsicott and Maushold quickly. Excadrill's Iron Head 4x super effective on Ninetales-Alola was the finishing blow. Gholdengo's self-imposed SpA drops from Make It Rain (falling 2 stages total) made it unable to break through despite Aurora Veil support. However, Mega Charizard Y's Drought was completely overridden by Ninetales-Alola's Snow Warning on Turn 3/4, negating the sun gameplan entirely — Charizard still performed thanks to raw SpA and Gholdengo's SpA drops, but the Mega's primary strategic purpose (enabling Solar Beam and sun-boosted Fire Blast) was nullified. Venusaur never entered play, making it a dead slot in this game.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent in a rematch: (1) Reconsider bringing Mega Charizard Y or any sun-dependent Pokémon — their Snow + Aurora Veil wall invalidates the sun archetype. If Charizard Y is kept, delay Mega until Snow is already cleared, or pivot to a non-sun Mega. (2) Venusaur is a dead card against Snow; consider replacing with a Pokémon that functions independently of weather — Scizor (Bullet Punch priority vs Ninetales/Whimsicott, Pursuit on Gholdengo) or Steelix (Stealth Rock + physical bulk) from the bench would add more. (3) Rotom-Wash should be brought over Venusaur: it threatens Ninetales-Alola with Freeze-Dry and checks Gholdengo's Make It Rain pivots. (4) Preserve Excadrill's Focus Sash for the Ninetales-Alola check; its Mold Breaker Iron Head is the single most important tool against this team. (5) Weavile's Life Orb + Pressure + Ice Shard remains excellent for Whimsicott and Ninetales removal.
reflections.notebook: OPPONENT TENDENCIES: Hyper-offensive Snow team. Ninetales-Alola sets Aurora Veil + Snow (LightClay likely). Whimsicott leads with Tailwind/Encore under Prankster, uses Focus Sash. Gholdengo walls special attacks, uses Make It Rain (drops user SpA 1 per hit) + Recover for sustain. Maushold uses Follow Me/Population Bomb as redirect fodder. Bench: Blastoise (WaterPulse/AuraSphere/Ice Beam), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (CloseCombat/FlareBlitz). STRATEGIC FACTS REVEALED: Aurora Veil + Snow makes their special side extremely bulky; Excadrill Iron Head is 4x on Ninetales-Alola; Gholdengo SpA self-drops make it fall off after 2 Make It Rain uses; Charizard-Mega-Y Drought does NOT override Ninetales-Alola Snow Warning (Snow overwrites); Weavile Ice Shard threatens Whimsicott and Ninetales-Alola heavily. PREP CONCLUSIONS: Sun-based core (Charizard Y + Venusaur) is a poor fit against Snow; swap Venusaur for a weather-independent or Snow-resistant pivot (Rotom-Wash, Scizor). Excadrill and Weavile are correct picks. Prioritize Excadrill's Focus Sash preservation for the Ninetales matchup. Do not Mega Charizard preemptively if Snow is still on the field.
